Mode of Instruction During
the Pandemic: An Analysis

Overview
• The most prominent disruption to education caused by the
pandemic was the interruption of in-person learning for thousands
of students.
• Mode of instruction can be broadly classified as:
• In-person
• Remote or Virtual
• Hybrid (a combination of in-person and remote)
• Questions over the efficacy of education that was not in-person
about.
• This presentation gives some initial insight into the impact of
mode of instruction on student learning.

Data
Data was provided by IDOE including
• ILEARN data in English/language arts and mathematics including
student demographic data
• Mode of Instruction data for students that was merged with ILEARN
data. Mode of instruction indicated three types:
• In-person
• Remote or Virtual
• Hybrid (a combination of in-person and remote)

Analyses on Mode of Instruction
• Student level descriptive statistics associated with ILEARN mode of
instruction including:
• Participation by mode of instruction disaggregated by academic and
demographic student groups.
• Student achievement and growth by Mode of instruction disaggregated by
academic and demographic student groups
• School level descriptive statistics associated with ILEARN mode of
instruction instruction:
• School level participation by mode of instruction
• School level academic impact by mode of instruction
• Identification of schools instructing students remotely who seemed to do a
remarkable job based upon ILEARN results

Summary of Individual Results
• In-person was the predominant mode of instruction followed by remote,
hybrid, and virtual school instruction. In-person and remote instruction
constituted more than 80% of the mode of instruction.
• There is not an insignificant amount of missing mode of instructions data
(approximately 15%). It is unlikely the missing data changes the findings
of the study.
• In-person instruction was, on average, the uniformly best mode of
instruction for students consistently leading to the highest learning rates
for students.
• Growth rates associated with remote instruction were very poor, especially
in mathematics.
• Ethnic minority students were much more likely to receive remote
instruction than white students.

Summary of School Results
• As in-person was the predominant mode of instruction, the vast majority
of schools in Indiana were in person.
• Nearly 50% of schools had greater than 90% of students in person
• Nearly 80% of schools had greater than 60% of students in person
• Conversely, there were a small minority of school in Indiana who were
mostly virtual.
• About 5% of schools had greater than 50% of students whose
mode of education was virtual
• As the following charts show, the 5% of schools having greater than
50% of student who mode of education was virtual tended to be larger
schools serving lower achieving students.

Summary of School Results
• An initial takeaway from these analyses is that the learning of students with remote
instruction is far less than learning of students receiving in-person instruction.
• The first attempt at screening for schools whose primary mode of instruction was
remote, who demonstrated good performance in 2019, and showed resilience in
their performance during the pandemic (i.e., modest to no impact) yielded few
schools
• Unfortunately, using this screener to try and find schools that were primarily
remote, who were good before and showed resilience in their performance during
the pandemic yielded few schools.
• A next approach to screening will investigate schools with a substantial number of
students who received remote instruction, whose remote students performance as
well as or better than in-person students, who demonstrated good performance in
2019, and were resilient in their performance during the pandemic.
